exact_actual_steps:
4.2 Let E be the independent marker process B, leaving the independent uniform seeds unconditioned. Its value space $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb Z}$ is standard Borel. Put $U=X_0^{n-1}$ and $V=\widehat X_0^{n-1}$. Independence in step 1.2 gives $P_{UE}=P_U\otimes P_E$, so $I_2(U;E)=D(P_U\otimes P_E\|P_U\otimes P_E)/\ln2=0$. Coordinate-swap invariance and the first-argument chain rule in [F5] now give
$$I_2(U;(V,E))=I_2((E,V);U)=I_2(E;U)+I_2(V;U\mid E)=0+I_2(U;V\mid E).$$
Expanding instead in the order $(V,E)$ gives $I_2(U;(V,E))=I_2(U;V)+I_2(U;E\mid V)\ge I_2(U;V)$. Thus $I_2(X_0^{n-1};\widehat X_0^{n-1})\le I_2(X_0^{n-1};\widehat X_0^{n-1}\mid E)$, using only nonnegative extended sums and the explicitly zero independent term. Conditional on E, outputs from distinct test-channel blocks are sampled independently according to $W_k$, and leftover outputs are deterministic. Enlarge the source window to include every source coordinate in a full length-$k$ block intersecting $[0,n-1]$, and enlarge the output to include each such full test-channel block output plus the leftover reconstructions inside the window. The original source and output windows are coordinate projections of these enlarged finite vectors, so [F6], applied conditionally on each marker realization, bounds the original information by the enlarged information. Conditional output entropy is subadditive across block outputs and leftover symbols. Given the enlarged source and E, the block outputs are independent and the leftover symbols are deterministic, so conditional output entropy is the sum of the block conditional entropies. Each length-$k$ block has the stationary source law followed by $W_k$, and hence contributes $I_k$ bits; each leftover symbol contributes at most $\log_2|\widehat{\mathcal X}|$ bits. There are at most $n/k+2$ intersecting channel blocks, and stationarity makes the expected number of leftover sites in the window $n\alpha$. Therefore $$ \frac1n I_2(X_0^{n-1};\widehat X_0^{n-1})\le\left(\frac1k+\frac2n\right)I_k+\alpha\log_2|\widehat{\mathcal X}|. $$ [A1, F1, F5, F6, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.2, given, algebra]

1.1 Fix a length-$n$ code, put $W=f_n(X^n)$, and write $\widehat X_i$ for the $i$th decoder output. Let $u_M$ be uniform on $[M]$. By [F13],
$$0\le D(P_W\|u_M)=\sum_{w:P_W(w)>0}P_W(w)\ln\frac{P_W(w)}{1/M}=\ln M-H(W),$$
so $\ln M\ge H(W)$. The conditional-mutual-information identity and nonnegativity in [F5] give $H(W)-H(W|Y^n)=I(W;Y^n)\ge0$ and
$$I(X^n;W|Y^n)=H(W|Y^n)-H(W|X^n,Y^n)\le H(W|Y^n),$$
because conditional entropy is nonnegative by its finite-sum definition [F12]. Combining these inequalities gives $\ln M\ge H(W)\ge H(W|Y^n)\ge I(X^n;W|Y^n)$. [F1, F5, F12, F13, algebra]

[F2] [[def-measure-theoretic-mutual-information]] and [[thm-mutual-information-chain-rule]] give $I((Z,V);U)=I(Z;U)+I(V;U\mid Z)$ as an extended nonnegative sum. By [[lem-kl-invariant-under-measurable-bijections]], swapping the two unconditioned coordinates sends the joint law and its product reference to the corresponding reversed laws; fixing a conditioning coordinate sends its same-marginal conditional-product reference to the reversed reference as well. Thus $I(U;V)=I(V;U)$ and $I(U;V\mid W)=I(V;U\mid W)$. Combining these symmetries with the stated first-argument rule proves
$$I(U;(Z,V))=I(U;Z)+I(U;V\mid Z).$$
For an additional standard-Borel W, apply this identity to the conditional law given $W=w$ for almost every w and integrate. [[thm-general-kl-chain-rule-for-standard-borel-kernels]], applied with the common W marginal, identifies the three integrals as
$$I(U;(Z,V)\mid W)=I(U;Z\mid W)+I(U;V\mid Z,W).$$
All integrations and rearrangements here concern nonnegative KL values; no possibly infinite term is subtracted.

1.1 Write $\delta_i=\mathbb E(X_i-Y_i)^2$, so $\sum_i\delta_i\le D$. Repeated use of [F2] expands $I_{\rm nat}(X^m;Y^m)$ as $\sum_i I_{\rm nat}(X_i;Y^m\mid X_1^{i-1})$. Put $W_i=X_1^{i-1}$. Reorder $Y^m$ as $(Y_i,Y_{[m]\setminus\{i\}})$ by the coordinate-bijection invariance in [F2]. Its derived second-argument conditional rule gives
$$I_{\rm nat}(X_i;Y^m\mid W_i)=I_{\rm nat}(X_i;Y_i\mid W_i)+I_{\rm nat}(X_i;Y_{[m]\setminus\{i\}}\mid W_i,Y_i)\ge I_{\rm nat}(X_i;Y_i\mid W_i),$$
by nonnegativity [F3]; the empty tuple has zero information. [A1, F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 Independence gives $P_{X_iW_i}=P_{X_i}\otimes P_{W_i}$, so $I_{\rm nat}(X_i;W_i)=0$ from the KL definition. The derived second-argument rule in [F2] gives
$$I_{\rm nat}(X_i;(W_i,Y_i))=0+I_{\rm nat}(X_i;Y_i\mid W_i)=I_{\rm nat}(X_i;Y_i\mid W_i).$$
A coordinate swap and the other expansion give
$$I_{\rm nat}(X_i;(W_i,Y_i))=I_{\rm nat}(X_i;(Y_i,W_i))=I_{\rm nat}(X_i;Y_i)+I_{\rm nat}(X_i;W_i\mid Y_i)\ge I_{\rm nat}(X_i;Y_i).$$
These identities remain valid when an information value is infinite, since only the explicitly zero term is removed and all other terms are nonnegative. Thus $I_{\rm nat}(X^m;Y^m)\ge\sum_i I_{\rm nat}(X_i;Y_i)$. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

u$ be probability measures on E, and let $K,L:Eightsquigarrow F$ be probability kernels. Let $P=\mu\ltimes K$ and $Q=
u\ltimes L$ be the joint probability laws defined by
$$P(C)=\int_E K(x,C_x)\,\mu(dx),\qquad Q(C)=\int_E L(x,C_x)\,
u(dx)$$
for product-measurable $C\subseteq E	imes F$. Then
$$D(P\|Q)=D(\mu\|
u)+\int_E D(K(x,\cdot)\|L(x,\cdot))\,\mu(dx)=D(\mu\|
u)+D_\mu(K\|L),$$
as an equality in $[0,+\infty]$. In particular, when $\mu=
u$, the joint KL is the conditional KL from [[def-conditional-kl-for-probability-kernels]].
